facts.text: Metro says its fixed-route city buses are low-floor with a deployable boarding ramp, a kneeling feature, wheelchair securement locations and priority seating at the front.
quote: Accessible Fixed Route Buses Did you know that Metro operates accessible buses on all city bus fixed routes? Accessibility features include:
Low floor buses with a boarding ramp that can be deployed A kneeling feature that lowers the bus closer to the curb Wheelchair securement locations Priority seating at the front of the bus

facts.text: Metro says bus stop announcements on its fixed-route buses are both audible and visual.
quote: Accessible Fixed Route Buses Did you know that Metro operates accessible buses on all city bus fixed routes? Accessibility features include:
Bus stop announcements that are both audible and visual

facts.text: Access is a shared-ride paratransit service for people whose disabilities prevent them from riding Metro buses; riders must apply and be approved first, which can take up to three weeks and includes an in-person functional skills assessment.
quote: Access is a shared-ride public transportation service, providing origin-to-destination transportation services for individuals whose disabilities prevent them from riding Metro buses. To use Access, you must first apply and be approved for service, a process that can take up to three weeks.
The application process includes an in-person functional skills assessment and interview.

facts.text: Access operates only within 3/4 mile of regular (non-express) Metro service and during Metro's regular hours; trips are reserved by phone, and riders get a 30-minute pickup window with a 5-minute driver wait.
quote: Hours of Operation: Same as Metro's Regular Service Hours Service Area: 3/4 mile of regular (non-express) Metro service Service Limitations: Service is not available beyond the designated service area or during hours when Metro's regular service is not operating.
Call Customer Care at 513-531-8888 to make a reservation.

After making your reservation you will be given a 30-minute “pickup window” and this is when the Access driver is scheduled to arrive. Be ready to travel at the beginning of your pickup window and make sure you are in an area where you can see or hear the bus when it arrives. The Access driver will wait 5 minutes. If you do not board within the 5-minute window, the bus will leave to pick up the next customer and you may be considered a no-show.

facts.text: On Access, a personal care attendant rides free; drivers secure mobility devices but cannot lift riders in or out of wheelchairs or scooters, and eating and drinking are prohibited on Access vehicles.
quote: Access’s goal is to accommodate all Paratransit riders. However, drivers are not allowed to:
Paratransit drivers will secure all mobility devices.
Eating, drinking and smoking are prohibited on all Access vehicles.
Lift you in and out of wheelchairs or scooters. You must provide your own Personal Care Attendant (PCA) or escort for assistance. A PCA can ride free of charge.

facts.text: Fare Deal ID cards give half-price fares on Metro fixed routes. Riders aged 65 or older qualify automatically but must provide proof of age; Medicare card holders of any age also qualify automatically. Riders with disabilities under 65 without Medicare must apply and be certified.
quote: Metro’s Fare Deal program allows eligible riders to obtain a Fare Deal identification card valid for half-price fares on Metro fixed-route trips.

Those 65 years-old and older are automatically eligible; proof of age is required. Medicare card holders of any age are also automatically eligible. Riders with disabilities who don’t have Medicare and are not 65 must submit an application and be certified to qualify for the program.

facts.text: Access paratransit passholders ride Metro fixed-route buses for half price.
quote: Access Paratransit passholders may ride Metro fixed-route service for half price.

facts.text: Service animals ride Metro buses with no extra fare.
quote: All service animals are allowed to ride Metro buses without paying an additional fare.

facts.text: Access offers free transportation to the functional skills assessment from locations within its service area. Book Access trips with Customer Care at 513-531-8888 or in the MyAccess app.
quote: Access does offer transportation to the functional skills assessment free of charge from all locations within the Access service area.
Call Customer Care at 513-531-8888 to make a reservation.
The MyAccess app is the new, convenient way for Metro Access riders to book, track, and manage their trips—all from their smartphone.

facts.text: Metro says visitors certified for paratransit in their hometown may qualify for temporary Access service, limited to 21 days. Contact eligibility at 513-632-7586 as far ahead as possible and provide current home-agency eligibility; Metro says more than 21 service days in a calendar year require its full application process.
quote: Visitors to the Metro service area who have been certified as eligible for paratransit services in their hometown may be eligible to receive temporary paratransit services from Access. This also applies to Access passengers who wish to travel to other cities that offer their own paratransit services. The temporary period is limited to 21 days of paratransit service.

Please contact the eligibility office at 513-632-7586 as far in advance as possible to inquire about temporary visitor service. Visitors must provide current ADA eligibility for paratransit service from the city, region, or jurisdiction in which they reside. Visitors who require more than 21 days of service in the calendar year will be required to apply and complete the full Access eligibility process.

facts.text: Metro says Access applications are no longer accepted by mail or fax. After submitting an application, call 513-632-7586 to schedule the in-person assessment.
quote: Access requires an eligibility application submitted, describing your disability or condition that prevents you from utilizing the fixed route service. Access no longer accepts applications by mail or fax. Applications are available in digital format or downloadable PDF. Your disability or condition must meet ADA requirements for certification. After submitting their application, applicants must call 513-632-7586 to schedule an in-person transportation skills assessment.

facts.text: Access assessments take place at 7000 Montgomery Road in Silverton. Bring any mobility aid you require; a complete application and valid photo ID are also required, or the assessment must be rescheduled.
quote: The application process includes an in-person functional skills assessment and interview. Assessments are conducted at 7000 Montgomery Road Silverton, OH 45236.
If an applicant requires the use of a mobility aid, the mobility aid must be brought to their functional skills assessment.

The assessment will not be processed without both a complete ADA Transportation Application and a valid photo ID. Applicants will need to reschedule their assessment appointment if they are unable to provide both items at the time of their appointment.

facts.text: Access drivers cannot enter your home, clear snow or objects from the approach, lock or unlock house doors, load or unload personal items, or carry groceries and packages.
quote: Drivers cannot enter your home.
Access’s goal is to accommodate all Paratransit riders. However, drivers are not allowed to:
Clear snow, ice or other objects from your steps, driveway or walkway. Lock or unlock house doors. Load or unload personal items. Carry groceries and packages.

facts.text: Metro says Access cannot serve a pickup or destination where its vehicle cannot maneuver safely. An alternative pickup address may be arranged; this is not a guarantee that a particular address can be served.
quote: If it is determined that a location you would like to travel to or from is not safe to maneuver in one of our paratransit vehicles, we will not be able to serve that location (e.g. dangerous double parking, required backing of the vehicle, low hanging branches, not safe area to board the vehicle, etc.). Arrangements may be made for an alternative pick-up address that is safer.

facts.text: Check the destination’s opening time before reserving Access: the driver cannot wait with you if it is closed when you arrive.
quote: Be aware of the opening and closing times of your destination to avoid waiting outside. If your destination is closed at the time you arrive, the Paratransit driver cannot wait with you until it opens.

facts.text: Metro says Access drivers help riders on and off the vehicle lift or steps, secure wheelchairs or scooters and fasten seatbelts. This boarding assistance does not include lifting a rider into or out of their mobility device.
quote: Access’s goal is to accommodate all Paratransit riders. However, drivers are not allowed to:
When your vehicle arrives, the driver will assist you on/off the vehicle lift or steps, secure your wheelchair or scooter, fasten your seatbelt and collect the fare.
Lift you in and out of wheelchairs or scooters. You must provide your own Personal Care Attendant (PCA) or escort for assistance. A PCA can ride free of charge.

facts.text: For an Access reservation, have your name or ID, travel date, pickup and destination addresses, required arrival time and return pickup time ready. Tell the receptionist about any companion or personal care attendant and special driver instructions.
quote: When making a reservation please have the following information. Your name or ID number. The date you would like to travel. The address of both pick up location and destination. The time you need to arrive at your destination. The time you need to be picked up for your return trip. Whether you will be traveling with a companion and / or personal care attendant. Special instructions for the driver.

facts.text: The Access page gives a $4.40 fare, with a dated increase effective July 16, 2025 alongside its older $4.00 line. Pay the exact fare in cash, Access tickets or a combination; Access tickets cannot pay fares on Metro fixed routes.
quote: Cost: $4.40 Dollars Per Ride
Access Fare Hamilton County: $4.00 (As of April 4, 2021).
Notice: Starting July 16, 2025, Access rides will increase to $4.40.
Access fares can be paid in any combination of cash and tickets equaling the exact fare. Access tickets cannot be accepted for fares on any Metro route.

facts.text: The Access contact list gives 800-750-0750 for TTY/Ohio Relay Service. The reservations line is separately listed as 513-531-8888.
quote: Access Reservations: 513-531-8888
TTY for hearing impaired/ Ohio Relay Service: 800-750-0750

facts.text: Following the functional skills assessment, Metro says applicants receive written notice of their Access eligibility decision within 21 days. An ineligibility notice includes the reasons and appeal-process information.
quote: Following the functional skills assessment, applicants will receive written notice of determination of eligibility within 21 days.
If an applicant is determined ineligible for Access services, their notice of determination provides specifics related to the determination and information of an appeals process.

facts.text: The branch has a free parking lot directly past the library on Scott Boulevard, but the library notes it may be full at times, especially during popular events; metered street parking (free after 4 pm and on weekends) and a fee-based garage are also nearby.
quote: Turn right on Scott Blvd. Our free parking is available in the lot on the left directly past the library. Parking: The Covington Library has a free parking lot for our visitors. Please note that free parking may not be available at all times, especially during popular events Metered parking and a fee-based parking garage are also available. Street meters are free after 4 pm and on weekends.

facts.text: TANK buses serve the Covington branch.
quote: TANK bus serves the Covington Library.

facts.text: The library system offers free monthly Homebound delivery of materials such as books, audiobooks, CDs and DVDs to Kenton County residents whose short- or long-term disability or medical condition keeps them from visiting.
quote: Homebound services are designed to offer library materials and programming to Kenton County residents with a short or long-term disability, or a medical condition that prevents them from visiting the Library .
Free deliveries of any available materials are made monthly. This includes books, CDs, audiobooks, DVDs, etc.

facts.text: All meeting rooms are described as accessible, with power outlets.
quote: All meeting rooms are accessible and have power outlets.

facts.text: The drive-thru closes one hour before the branch.
quote: Library drive-thru closes one hour before the branch.

facts.text: The branch lists all-day Thanksgiving closures on November 26–27, 2026, and Christmas closures on December 24–25. Check its current calendar before travelling.
quote: Thanksgiving and Friday After Thursday, November 26, 2026 - Friday, November 27, 2026 Closed All Day Christmas Eve & Christmas Day Thursday, December 24, 2026 - Friday, December 25, 2026 Closed All Day

facts.text: Campbell County residents who can't visit the library because of a temporary or permanent illness or disability can get materials delivered at home, or by mail for free.
quote: If you are a resident of Campbell County and cannot visit the library because of temporary or permanent illness or disability, you are eligible for our home delivery service. Materials available for delivery include regular print books, large print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs. Materials are selected based on your reading interests and needs. The Adult Outreach Services Assistant will deliver the materials to your home on a specified day. You may also sign up to have your materials delivered by mail for free.

facts.text: The library helps patrons sign up for the free Kentucky Talking Book service, for anyone unable to read because of a visual or physical limitation, and the national program of braille and audio materials sent by postage-free mail.
quote: Through a national network of cooperating libraries, the NLS administers a free library program of braille and audio materials circulated to eligible borrowers in the United States by postage-free mail. Kentucky Talking Books Talking Book Service is available through the Kentucky Talking Book Library. This service is provided free of charge to anyone unable to read because of a visual or physical limitation.
If you are interested in signing up for any of the free services below or would like more information, please call our Adult Outreach Services Assistant at 859-572-5035, ext. 352.

facts.text: For curbside pickup at Newport, place a hold and wait for a phone, text, email or postal notification. The item must also show as Held in the account. Call or email the library if you need help accessing the account or placing the hold.
quote: You can call or email us if you need help accessing your account or placing a hold. Search for an item in our catalog and click "Request Item" to place it on hold. Wait for a phone call, text, email or postal mail notifying you that your holds are ready for pickup. Follow instructions for curbside pickup below. Picking Up Items You will be notified by phone, text, email or postal mail when your holds are available for curbside pickup. Please note that your holds are not ready for pickup until you receive a notification and the items are marked as "Held" in your account.

facts.text: Use a designated curbside parking space, then call the number on its sign with your name, library card number and space number. If no one answers, call again rather than leaving voicemail. Stay in the vehicle; staff place items inside, preferably in the trunk.
quote: Park in one of the parking spots that are designated for curbside pickup. Let us know that you are outside by calling the number listed on the parking spot's sign. We will need your name, library card number and parking spot number. If a staff member doesn't answer, do not leave a voicemail message. Please call back until a staff member answers. Remain in your vehicle. A staff member will place your items directly in your vehicle, preferably into your trunk.

facts.text: Curbside pickup requires a current physical library card; a digital-only card does not qualify.
quote: Curbside pickup is available for current physical library card holders. The service is not available for digital library card holders.

facts.text: Holds remain available for seven days after the ready notification. Someone else may collect them if they have your library card number.
quote: You will have seven days to pick up your holds. Q: What if the parking spots designated for curbside pickup are full? A: If the parking spots are full, please park in another area of the parking lot until one is available. We will only deliver items to vehicles parked in the designated spots. Q: Who can pick up my items? A: Anyone may pick up your items. They must have your library card number in order to do so. Staff will not release items to those without a library card number.
Q: How long will I have to pick up my holds once I have been notified that they are ready? A: You will have seven days to pick up your holds.

facts.text: If all curbside spaces are occupied, wait elsewhere in the lot until one opens. Staff deliver only to vehicles in the designated spaces.
quote: If the parking spots are full, please park in another area of the parking lot until one is available. We will only deliver items to vehicles parked in the designated spots.

facts.text: Items can be returned inside or to the red return bins outside the branches. The page does not give the outdoor bin’s slot height or reach measurements.
quote: Items may be returned inside or by using the red item return bins that are outside each of our branches.

facts.text: For event accommodations, the district asks for at least 72 hours’ notice by emailing access@cc-pl.org or calling extension 8 at the local branch.
quote: Please email access@cc-pl.org or call ext. 8 at your local branch at least 72 hours prior to an event to arrange for accommodation.

facts.text: To arrange adult outreach, call 859-572-5035, extension 352. Home-delivery materials include regular and large-print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs; selection follows the reader’s interests and needs.
quote: If you'd like to set up one of these services, call our Adult Outreach Services Assistant at 859-572-5035, ext. 352.
Materials available for delivery include regular print books, large print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs. Materials are selected based on your reading interests and needs.

facts.text: Newport’s Kinsella Community Room is on the main floor; the Presidents Room is on the lower level. The district’s meeting-room policy identifies those floors but does not describe elevator operation or door widths.
quote: Newport has two large meeting rooms: the main floor Kinsella Community Room holds 65 and the lower level Presidents Room holds 85.

facts.text: Meeting-room reservations require an application and approval before the meeting, may be made up to three months ahead and are held for only 15 minutes after the reserved time. The person reserving a room must be at least 18.
quote: The application (available online) for use of library facilities must be completed each time a meeting room is requested. The application must be received and approved by the library director (or designee) prior to the scheduled meeting. Reservations may be made up to three months in advance. Reservations will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. A maximum of three meetings may be scheduled and active at a time across all branches. The library shall be notified 48 hours in advance in case of cancellations or changes. Rooms will only be held for 15 minutes past the reservation time.
Individuals reserving the meeting room must be at least 18 years of age.

facts.text: Study rooms are reserved in two-hour blocks, extendable to four hours if no one is waiting. Public meetings must end at least 15 minutes before closing; private social events must end at least 30 minutes before closing.
quote: All meetings must be within regular operating hours. Public meetings must end a minimum of fifteen minutes prior to closing. Private social events must end a minimum of 30 minutes prior to closing. Study rooms are reserved in two (2) hour blocks. This time may be extended up to four (4) hours if others are not waiting to use the room.

facts.text: The Pavilion is at 6200 Pfeiffer Road. Its driving directions describe a long driveway on the north side of Pfeiffer Road, just west of I-71; this does not establish a step-free pedestrian route.
quote: The TriHealth Fitness and Health Pavilion is accessible by turning onto a long driveway located on the north side of Pfieffer Road, just a few hundred feet west of I-71.
6200 Pfeiffer Road Cincinnati, OH 45242

facts.text: Membership includes three heated pools: an indoor 25-meter lap pool, an indoor 2,000-square-foot warm-water therapy pool and a seasonal outdoor leisure pool. The outdoor pool is described as zero-entry; that description does not cover the indoor pools.
quote: The TriHealth Fitness and Health Pavilion offers access to three heated pools, which are included in your membership: Indoor 25-meter lap pool Indoor 2,000 square-foot warm water therapy pool, suited for arthritis relief and rehabilitation Seasonal, zero-entry outdoor leisure pool

facts.text: The pool page lists men’s and women’s locker rooms, each with a sauna, steam room and whirlpool, and says gender-neutral rooms are also available. It does not describe toilet clearances or adult changing equipment.
quote: Additionally, we have fully equipped men's and women's locker rooms each with a sauna, steam room and whirlpool. Gender neutral rooms also are available.

facts.text: The Pavilion’s personal-assistant policy says staff are not permitted to physically assist members using equipment or facilities. Members who need this help must plan their own assistance through the personal-assistant process.
quote: For members' and employees' safety, the Pavilion staff are not permitted to physically assist members with the use of any equipment or facilities on the Pavilion premises. Because of this, the Pavilion offers a Personal Assistant Program to benefit members who may require additional assistance.

facts.text: A member must identify their personal assistant, and management must approve that person as capable of providing adequate assistance throughout the visit. The form includes member and assistant agreements.
quote: I realize that it is my responsibility to identify someone who will serve as my Personal Assistant and that this person must be approv ed by management as someone capable of providing me with adequate assistance at all times during my Pavilion visit.
THIS PAGE TO BE COMPLETED BY MEMBER
THIS PAGE TO BE COMPLETED BY PERSONAL ASSISTANT

facts.text: An approved personal assistant agrees to remain with the member at all times on the premises and check in at the service desk before every visit; the assistant check-in has no fee.
quote: I will remain with Member at all times while on the premises
I am required to check in at the service desk before each visit (no fee required).

facts.text: For the seasonal outdoor pool, inclement weather triggers closure until 30 minutes after the last lightning or thunder. During a weather closure, members may use the indoor pools during open swim, but not during classes.
quote: In case of inclement weather the outdoor pool will close and will reopen 30 minutes after the last sight of lightning or thunder. If the outdoor pool is closed due to inclement weather, members may swim indoors during open swim time (not during classes).

facts.text: Member Services can be reached at 513-246-2611 to discuss visit arrangements. Its published hours may change on holidays.
quote: Member Services: 513 246 2611 Monday - Thursday 8:30 a.m. - 6:30 p.m. Friday 8:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m. Saturday - Sunday 8:30 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. Hours subject to change on holidays

facts.text: The Winton Road branch is at 9601 Winton Road; call 513-521-7112 about the exact pool and session you intend to use.
quote: Powel Crosley, Jr. YMCA 9601 Winton Road Cincinnati, Ohio 45231 (513) 521-7112

facts.text: The branch’s back-to-school table says the baby pool is closed for the season and the outdoor pool is for lap swimming only. The table has no year, so confirm current seasonal arrangements with the branch.
quote: Back to School Swim Baby pool - Closed for the season Outdoor Pool - open for lap swim only

facts.text: The pool-schedule page says reservations open 48 hours before class time through the MyY app or by logging in to a member account.
quote: Reservations open 48 hours before class time and can be made on the MyY App or by logging in to your member account .

facts.text: The outdoor bubble-pool lap-swimming table requires reservations. The indoor lap-pool table says Monday–Friday is closed for open swim, while a separate indoor-waterpark table offers family splash sessions. These are separate listings, not evidence that all indoor swimming is closed.
quote: Outdoor Bubble Pool - Lap Swimming (Reservations Required) Monday-Friday 5-10 am & 11 am-7:45 pm Saturday 7 am - 5:45 pm Sunday 12 pm - 5:45 pm Indoor Pool- Lap Swimming (Reservation Required) Monday - Friday Closed for open swim Indoor Waterpark - Family Open Splash Monday - Friday 10 am - 1 pm & 5 pm - 7:45 pm Saturday 9 am - 5:45 pm Sunday 12 pm - 5:45 pm All children under 16

facts.text: Children under 16 must wear a swim band. Yellow and green bands require a completed swim test and must be presented on each visit.
quote: All children under 16 must wear a swim band. Yellow and green bands require a completed swim test and must be presented at each visit.

facts.text: The YMCA of Greater Cincinnati says visiting Nationwide Members should identify themselves at the Welcome Desk for barcode check-in. They cannot reserve classes or lap swim, but may try to attend a class that is not full. Confirm pool availability directly.
quote: For participating YMCAs, let our Welcome Desk know you are scanning in as a Nationwide Member and we will switch the check-in for your barcode to check that you are up-to-date.
Nationwide Members are welcome to use our facilities. Class or lap swim reservations are not available but you are welcome to try to attend if a class isn't full.

facts.text: Under the shared guest policy, all guests must be registered in Daxko and complete a waiver before entry. Guests aged 16 or older need photo ID on their first visit; individual guests may visit at most three times per calendar year.
quote: All guests must be entered in Daxko and waiver complete prior to entry.
All guests 16 years of age and older must present a photo ID upon their first visit. Individual guests are welcome to visit the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati a maximum of 3 times per calendar year.

facts.text: The shared FAQ allows members aged 18 or older to bring guests. Guests using a six-punch guest pass must stay with an active YMCA member at all times. It says day passes are not sold and guests must be accompanied by a member or have a complimentary guest pass; ask the branch which guest arrangement applies.
quote: Members 18 years of age and older may bring in guests.
Guests using a “6-punch guest pass” must be accompanied at ALL times by an active YMCA Member.
Can I purchase a day pass? No. All guests must be accompanied by a member or have a complimentary guest pass.

facts.text: The shared FAQ provides day-use lockers for members and guests at every YMCA of Greater Cincinnati location. Bring your own lock and remove it after each visit; overnight storage requires a rented locker, whose availability must be checked with the branch. Locker reach and changing-room layouts are not specified.
quote: Lockers are provided for your convenience at all YMCA of Greater Cincinnati locations. Lockers are for day use by members and guests.

It is important to secure your personal belongings by bringing your own lock and removing it at the end of each visit. Items cannot be left overnight unless you have rented the locker. Check with your local YMCA branch to see if locker rentals are available.

facts.text: To join, the shared FAQ offers help from branch member-service staff or a phone appointment with a member engagement specialist. Online joining is also offered, with the membership card collected on the first branch visit.
quote: First, you can visit your local Y and any of our member service staff will be happy to help you get started.
Or, you can call your local Y to schedule an appointment with a member engagement specialist who will walk you through the joining process.
You can also join online and receive your membership card when you first use the branch.

facts.text: Silverlake is at 301 Kenton Lands Road in Erlanger; the club’s contact number is 859-426-7777.
quote: 859-426-7777 301 Kenton Lands Rd, Erlanger, KY 41018

facts.text: To use Silverlake, you must be a member, a guest or a participant in a facility program or event. Membership cards are used for entry.
quote: To use the facilities of Silverlake you must be a member, a guest or a participant in a program or event of the facility. Upon payment of the required fee membership cards will be issued to each member and must be used to gain access.

facts.text: Guests must accompany a member; guests under 18 must accompany an adult member over 18. The same guest is limited to one visit per 30 days, with a $15 guest fee. More than two guests requires prior arrangement, some days may restrict guests, and Water Park guests are permitted only Monday–Friday.
quote: Guests must be accompanied by a member. Guests under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult member (over 18). The same guest is limited to 1 visit per 30 days. $15 Guest fee applies for all guests. If member is bringing more than 2 guests at one time, it must be arranged with membership representative prior to arriving at club. Guests may be limited or not allowed on certain days. Guests are permitted at the Water Park only Monday - Friday.

facts.text: A fee-waiving guest pass requires a local resident aged at least 23 who is visiting for the first time, and must be arranged through a membership representative at least 24 hours ahead. Blackout dates apply.
quote: A guest pass, waiving the guest fee, can be obtained from a membership representative provided the following conditions are met: Guest is a local resident, 23 years of age or older. Guest is a first time visitor to Silverlake. Pass must be arranged through the membership representative 24 hours in advance. Black out dates do apply.

facts.text: The indoor aquatic-center page lists direct access from the locker rooms, but does not give doorway widths, thresholds or pool-entry equipment.
quote: Direct Access from Locker Rooms

facts.text: The club provides family locker rooms for families with opposite-gender children. Day-use locker contents must be removed when leaving; monthly rental lockers are available for items left at the club.
quote: Family Locker Rooms are provided for those with opposite gender children.

Daily use lockers are available to all members. All contents must be removed upon leaving the club. These lockers are emptied each evening by club personnel. Lockers are available on a monthly rental basis for those wishing to leave their things at the club.

facts.text: Members using the pool must first check in at the front desk. Lap lanes are reserved for people aged 18 or older unless a lifeguard approves otherwise; pool hours before 11 a.m. are reserved for members aged 18 or older except programmed activities.
quote: Any member using the pool must first check in at the front desk.
Lap lanes are reserved for those 18 years of age and over unless approved by a lifeguard.
Pool hours before 11 a.m. each day are reserved for those members 18 years of age and over. Programmed activity is an exception.

facts.text: Activity hours vary by season and may change for weather or advisories; current area-hour handouts are available at the front desk. Events and programs may restrict parts of the facility, and Clippers practice uses part of the pool during operating hours.
quote: Hours for the different activities in the facility will vary from season to season. Hours for the different areas of the facility will be available at the front desk in the form of a hand out. ALL HOURS ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE. Hours may be altered due to weather or advisories. PLEASE CHECK WITH THE FRONT DESK ON A REGULAR BASIS REGARDING HOURS OF OPERATION.

Silverlake reserves the right to schedule tournaments, exhibitions, parties, programs, rentals, leagues, and other events. Members may not be able to use all or part of the facility prior to and/or during these times. Silverlake will use its best efforts to notify Members of any such limitation of use as far in advance as is possible. A part of the pool will be used for the practice of the Clippers swim program during the operating time of the facility.

facts.text: The indoor aquatic center lists a lap pool, a warm-water pool, a water slide and splash features with separate activity times. The page does not promise a quiet session; consult the activity schedule when planning around water-play activity.
quote: 50 Meter Olympic Size Lap Pool 2500 Sq Foot Warm Water Pool & indoor Waterpark Open Year Round Swim America Group Lessons Lap Swimming All Day Group Exercise Classes (Shallow Deep & Warm Water) Aqua Spin Warm Water Hydro Therapy Classes 100 Ft Adrenaline Slide Water Works & Geyser Splash Area Paddle Boats Direct Access from Locker Rooms

Waterworks Splash Tower & Geysers Mon & Wed 12:30PM - 7:00PM Tues & Thurs 12:30PM - 5:30PM* Fri 12:30PM - 8:30PM Sat 11:00AM - 5:30PM Sun 11:00AM - 4:30PM *closed for swim lessons Adrenaline Water Slide Mon & Wed 4:00PM - 7:00P Fri 4:00PM - 8:30PM Sat 11:00AM - 5:30PM Sun 11:00AM - 4:30PM Paddle Boats Fri 4:00PM - 7:00PM Sat 11:00AM - 5:30PM Sun 11:00AM - 4:30PM

facts.text: The currently linked November 2026 fitness schedule gives the club address as 401 Farrell Court, Cincinnati, and phone 513-347-1400.
quote: 401 Farrell Court Cincinnati, OH 45233 513-347-1400

facts.text: Bayley describes its fitness offering as serving adults in the greater community as well as on campus. Ask the club about current membership eligibility, prices and guest access before visiting; the page does not specify a minimum age or day-pass conditions.
quote: With inspiring programs, first-rate amenities, and a welcoming neighborhood, we offer only the best for adults in the greater community and on campus.

facts.text: The fitness page lists an aquatics center, indoor walking track, strength/cardio center and locker rooms. It does not describe a step-free entrance route, lift equipment or assisted changing facilities.
quote: Aquatics Center Indoor Walking Track Strength and Cardio Center Group Fitness Classes Personal Training Locker Rooms

facts.text: The November 2026 schedule requires registration for every class and limits class size to avoid overcrowding. Sign-ups open 72 hours before each class. If a place opens, the next person on the waitlist is automatically enrolled and notified; remove yourself from the class list if you cannot attend.
quote: Registration for all classes is required! All classes are available to attend. Due to popularity of classes and to avoid overcrowding class size is limited. • Sign ups for classes will open 72 hours before each class starts. • Waitlist: if a position opens and you are next on the waitlist, you will be automatically enrolled in the class and notified accordingly.
IF YOU CAN NO LONGER ATTEND THE CLASS, IT IS IMPERATIVE THAT YOU TAKE YOUR NAME OFF OF THAT CLASS LIST.

facts.text: The pool closes 15 minutes before the fitness facility. The November 2026 pool schedule prohibits individual workouts and whirlpool use during scheduled classes, so check the pool timetable before planning an independent swim.
quote: (Pool closes 15 mins. prior to facility)
INDIVIDUAL WORKOUTS AND /OR WHIRLPOOL USE NOT PERMITTED DURING SCHEDULED CLASSES

facts.text: The November 2026 schedule lists the club closed on Thanksgiving, Thursday November 26, and open 8 a.m.–6:30 p.m. on Friday November 27. These holiday hours differ from the usual Friday opening.
quote: Thursday 11/26 Closed Happy Thanksgiving Friday 11/27 8:00 am -6:30pm
Friday 6:30am-6:30pm

facts.text: The class guide distinguishes activity levels and describes Chair Pilates+ as a seated-and-standing format. A class name containing “chair” does not mean the whole class is seated; discuss your requirements with the instructor.
quote: Bayley Fitness Club classes are designated by level of activity and type of activity.
Chair Pilates+ [Mon & Fri 11:20am] [S,F,B,MB] Seated & standing format for core based Pilates exercises for abs, back & hips.

facts.text: MetroNow! is open to the public, but every trip must be booked beforehand through its app or 513-551-5555. Book a child or companion as an additional rider too.
quote: No. While MetroNow! is completely open to the public, you must schedule a trip beforehand. Trips can be scheduled via the MetroNow app, or by calling 513-551-5555. If you are bringing a child or companion, their ride must also be scheduled.

facts.text: Request “Less Walking” for curb-to-curb service. Metro directs riders who have difficulty walking or use a wheelchair to select this option; “Less Waiting” uses corner-to-corner pickup and may involve walking a block or two.
quote: You can either request “Less Walking” which will provide curb-to-curb service or “Less Waiting” which will provide corner-to-corner service depending on your needs.
Note: “Less Waiting” or corner-to-corner service is the faster option if you’re able and willing to walk a block or two to a designated pick-up point.
If you have difficulty walking or use a mobility aid such as a wheelchair, please select “Less Walking” for curb-to-curb.

facts.text: Metro says each MetroNow! vehicle has space for two mobility aids, such as wheelchairs or strollers. Indicate wheelchair use in your account settings.
quote: Yes, each MetroNow! vehicle has onboard space for two mobility aids (such as wheelchairs or strollers). Let us know you will be traveling with a wheelchair in your account settings.

facts.text: Packages are permitted aboard MetroNow!, but may not occupy a seat. Operators are not permitted to help with packages.
quote: Yes, you may bring packages onboard MetroNow! vehicles; however, packages may not take up a seat, and operators are not permitted to assist customers with packages.

facts.text: The page’s launched-zone heading lists Bond Hill/Roselawn, Springdale/Sharonville, Northgate/Mt. Healthy, Forest Park/Pleasant Run and Blue Ash/Montgomery. Its FAQ still describes Bond Hill/Roselawn as future service; confirm exact pickup and destination coverage rather than relying on a neighborhood name.
quote: The Bond Hill/Roselawn zone has officially launched! This latest addition joins the existing MetroNow! zones in Springdale/Sharonville, Northgate/Mt. Healthy, Forest Park/Pleasant Run, and Blue Ash/Montgomery.
Once completely rolled out, MetroNow! will serve the following additional Hamilton County communities: Monfort Heights/Finneytown Bond Hill/Roselawn

facts.text: The app asks for pickup and destination addresses or map pins. It displays an “out of zone” message when the destination is outside the service zone; confirm coverage before planning a connection.
quote: Add your origin location address or adjust the pin to set it. Click “Confirm.” Add your destination address or adjust the pin, then click “Set Destination.” If the destination is outside the service zone, you'll receive an "out of zone" message.

facts.text: Published MetroNow! hours are weekdays 6 a.m.–10 p.m. and weekends 8 a.m.–9 p.m. Its holiday policy uses weekend service on New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas.
quote: Weekdays: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. | Weekends: 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
MetroNow! operates weekend service in observance of the following holidays: New Year’s Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Day Christmas Day

facts.text: MetroNow! lists a $2.50 fare. Its FAQ says Fare Deal, MVP and other Metro discount cards, fixed-route passes and transfers are not accepted for this service.
quote: $2.50 Dollars Per Ride
At this time, MetroNow! does not accept Fare Deal, MVP or any other Metro discount program cards. This includes transfers and passes from regular Metro fixed-route service.

facts.text: The MetroNow! app is offered in English and Spanish.
quote: The app is available in both English and Spanish.

facts.text: Metro’s child-seat policy makes riders responsible for bringing a seat that meets local requirements. Drivers may refuse a ride without it; Metro does not provide seats or operator help with installation.
quote: Metro requires car seats for children based on applicable local laws. Riders are responsible for providing a car seat that meets local requirements, and drivers may refuse rides if a car seat is not provided. Four seats in each vehicle are equipped with child safety seat hooks. Car seats will not be provided and operators may not assist with installation.

facts.text: The Mason store lists 7200 Mason Montgomery Road, daily hours of 6 a.m.–9 p.m. and phone 513-229-2500. Confirm holiday hours before travelling.
quote: Hours Mon - Sun: 6:00AM - 9:00PM Location 7200 Mason Montgomery Road Mason, OH 45040 Contact Us Send us a message Or call us at (513) 229-2500

facts.text: Mason’s Culinary Center is on the mezzanine level at the same store address; its contact number is 513-229-2510. The location description does not explain an elevator or step-free route.
quote: Mason Location 7200 Mason Montgomery Road Mason, Ohio 45040 513-229-2510 Located on mezzanine level.

facts.text: For private Culinary Center events, DLM says tables and chairs can be repositioned. Discuss the needed arrangement when booking; this is not a measured-clearance or step-free-access guarantee.
quote: Plus, tables and chairs can be repositioned to best fit your needs.
Mason 7200 Mason Montgomery Rd. Mason, Ohio 45040 (513) 229-2510 Located on mezzanine level inside DLM Mason.

facts.text: The Mason page offers frittata orders in-store or by phone for pickup. It does not describe vehicle handoff or grocery curbside collection.
quote: Frittatas
Get a delicious start to your day and order yours in-store or via phone for pick-up.

facts.text: The Campus Recreation Center lists its address as 2820 Bearcat Way and phone 513-556-0604. It is on UC’s Uptown West Campus.
quote: About the CRC 2820 Bearcat Way Cincinnati, OH 45219 513-556-0604
Cincinnati’s Campus Recreation Center (CRC) is a state-of-the-art fitness and recreation facility on its Uptown West Campus.

facts.text: Community members may buy memberships for themselves and their families. To join, bring photo ID or a Bearcat Card and a credit or debit card to Member Services for help with the application.
quote: UC faculty and staff (current and retired), alumni and community members are also eligible to purchase memberships for themselves and their families.
Bring your photo ID or Bearcat Card and a credit or debit card for payment.
Come in to the Member Services Desk at the Campus Recreation or Fitness Center at CARE/Crawley and our Member Services Team will walk you through the application and sign-up process.

facts.text: Except in an emergency, members must enter and leave the CRC through the main lobby. The policy does not describe that entrance’s thresholds or door controls.
quote: Except in the case of an emergency, members must enter and exit the Campus Recreation Center through the main lobby.

facts.text: UC requires a valid physical photo ID at Member Services for facility access; pictures and photocopies are not accepted.
quote: All individuals must present a valid, physical photo ID (no pictures or photocopies) at the Member Services Desk to obtain access to the facility.

facts.text: The leisure pool has a zero-depth entry and a maximum depth of 3.5 feet. This description is specific to the leisure pool, not the lap pool or hot tub.
quote: The shallow-water Leisure Pool has a zero-depth entry with a maximum depth of 3.5 feet and is typically 84 degrees.

facts.text: The pool page lists lap-pool closure every Wednesday 8 a.m.–noon and leisure-pool cleaning every Monday 8 a.m.–noon. Lane availability changes during the day because of practices and meets; check the lane schedule.
quote: Lane availability changes throughout the day - click the hotbutton below to view lane availability by day.
The pool also plays host to our UC Swim and Dive teams for practices and meets.
Note: The Lap Pool is closed every Wednesday 8 a.m. - 12 p.m.
Note: the Leisure Pool is closed for cleaning every Monday 8 a.m. - 12 p.m.

facts.text: UC’s locker-room rules offer family changing rooms for members with small children of the opposite sex. Children aged four or older may not enter the opposite-sex locker room. Adult assisted-changing equipment is not described.
quote: Children 4 years of age and older may not enter the locker room of the opposite sex. Family changing rooms are available for members with small children of the opposite sex. Please use discretion when bringing younger children of the opposite sex into the locker room.

facts.text: UC’s single-occupancy restroom directory lists CRC rooms including 0222A–0222D, 0M300B–0M300C, 1223 and 1224. It marks rooms 3356, 4356, 5356 and 6356 as student-only. Confirm the route and permission to enter; the directory does not establish toilet dimensions or changing equipment.
quote: Single Occupancy Restroom Locations
*All room numbers followed by an asterisk are only accessible to UC students (not the entire UC community)

facts.text: Day-use lockers are free and first-come. UC describes built-in combination locks in CRC locker rooms and at gym courts; ask Member Services which lock is needed for your chosen locker type.
quote: There is no fee for day-use lockers; they can be utilized on a first-come, first-served basis.

When using a locker at the Campus Recreation Center , a member will either use the built-in combination lock (in locker rooms and at gym courts) or use a personal lock (fitness floor and climbing wall) depending on locker type.
Visit the Member Services Desk for locker rental and towel service.

facts.text: UC names Campus Green and Woodside as the closest garages to the CRC. Proximity does not establish a step-free garage-to-lobby route.
quote: The Campus Recreation Center (CRC) is located in the center of campus, giving visitors several parking options. Campus Green and Woodside garages are the closest to the CRC.

facts.text: Parking is not included automatically with recreation membership. The member-parking option is available to community, affiliate and alumni members and their spouses, domestic partners and legal dependents; UC students, faculty and staff buy parking through Parking Services.
quote: Please note that parking is not automatically included with your membership. However, it is available for Community, Affiliate and Alumni members, as well as their spouses, domestic partners and legal dependents.
UC students, faculty and staff must purchase parking through UC Parking Services .

facts.text: For a Campus Rec parking card, scan in rather than taking a ticket so the card can scan out. The card covers three hours once daily while using recreation facilities; additional fees start after three hours and are charged at exit.
quote: You must scan the card in to be able to later scan out (do not pull a ticket on entry). Hold card under red barcode reader (see photo at the top of this page) to enter/exit the garage.
Each card entitles the designated permit holder to 3 hours of parking once per day while using Campus Rec facilities.
Additional fees will automatically begin after 3 hours and will be charged at exit.

facts.text: On game days, recreation members must use Campus Green Garage and show their card to the parking attendant; parking may be limited. For entry or exit trouble, press HELP on the card reader and report any error code to Member Services or 513-556-0604.
quote: Parking may be limited on game days, but members coming to work out can access the garage by showing their card to the Parking Services Attendant. Members must park in Campus Green Garage on game days.

If you have trouble entering or exiting the parking garage at the gate, press the HELP button on the card reader. If your pass did not work at the gate, please make sure to read the error code on the screen at the gate and let the Member Services Staff know about the issue at the desk or call 513-556-0604.

facts.text: A separate UC building-directory record identifies the Campus Recreation Center at 2840 Bearcat Way. Confirm the arrival point with recreation staff before travelling.
quote: Name: Campus Recreation Center (CRC) Address: 2840 Bearcat Way, Cincinnati OH 45219 Building Code: RECCENTER Campus: WEST
